newsitem.title: USA: Conservationists in N.E. Electric bid-report.
newsitem.headline: Conservationists in N.E. Electric bid-report.

text.p: A conservation group has teamed up with a Virginia power company in the bidding for New England Electric System's 18 power plants, the Boston Globe reported on Monday.
The Conservation Law Foundation of Boston and AES Corp formed the unusual alliance out of the common desire to close five of the 18 plants, the Globe said.
"The potential environmental benefits are off the charts," foundation director Douglas Foy told the newspaper.
"If we could figure out a way to help somebody buy those plants and close them, we could get results we could never hope for in the regulatory process," he added.
The alliance is one of twenty-five suitors who have submitted bids for New England Electric's 18 non-nuclear generating plants up for sale.
A select group of bidders will be asked to submit formal, binding bids for the plants, which have a book value of $1.2 billion, by the end of June.

Under the partnership, AES will provide most of the capital while Conservation Law would do "innovative financing" to pay for environmental benefits, such as dismantling closed plants, the Globe said. The closed plant sites could be redeveloped or cleaner gas plants could be built.
"Restructuring has really provided a lot of opportunity to do the cleanup that has eluded us up to now," AES chairman Roger Sant told the newspaper.
